puzzleDifficulty.description: Which puzzle each round serves, by edge count (lines to draw: 4-16 over the 60 puzzles). -1 (default; any negative value) keeps the game's own order, round N = puzzle N (4 lines in round 1, 11-16 in rounds 40-60). 0-1 is a quantile of edge count: each round serves one of the 10 puzzles nearest that rank, cycling as rounds advance (0: 4-9 lines, 0.25: 10-11, 0.5: 11-12, 0.75: 12-13, 1: 13-16). More lines are harder. Takes effect from the next puzzle; the puzzle in play and its retries do not change.
puzzleDifficulty.adjustment_guide: The main difficulty lever. Start around 0.3-0.5 once it is used; raise by about 0.25 after several TRY_SOLVED on the first or second try, lower by 0.25 after repeated TRY_FAILED or TRY_ABANDON on one round. -1 returns to the game's own order.

snapRadius.description: How close, in game units, the pointer must pass to a star for the line to connect (a star's white disc has a radius of 16). 30 is the game's own value. 15 means the pointer has to cross the star itself, so drawing needs precision; 45 is forgiving, but sweeping past a neighbouring star that has an open line from the current one can then capture it. Applies immediately.
snapRadius.adjustment_guide: A motor-precision lever, separate from the puzzle logic. Keep 30-45 for relax and for players whose TRY_FAILED come quickly after TRY_START (slips rather than wrong plans); lower to 20-25 for focus. Change by about 5 at a time.

startHint.description: 1 rings in yellow the two stars a solution has to start from (the stars with an odd number of lines); in the 20 puzzles where every star has an even number of lines any star works, so none is ringed. 0 (default) shows no hint. Applies to the puzzle in play and every later one.
startHint.adjustment_guide: Turn on (1) after repeated TRY_FAILED on one round or for relax; keep off (0) for planning and deduction practice, since finding the start is the key insight.

adjustment_instructions:
Star Puzzles is a one-stroke puzzle: each round shows a figure of stars joined by lines, and the player drags from star to star to draw over every line exactly once without lifting the pointer. A round has unlimited tries and no timer. Events: LEVEL_START (level = round), TRY_START (vertex = start star, connections = its open lines), TRY_FAILED (stuck before all lines are drawn), TRY_SOLVED, TRY_ABANDON (restart or home mid-try), LEVEL_QUIT. When puzzleDifficulty is 0-1, `level` is the round number, not the puzzle's position in the game's list.
Levers: puzzleDifficulty picks puzzles by edge count (-1 = the game's own order; 0 = fewest lines, 1 = most; higher = harder); snapRadius sets how close the pointer must pass to a star (lower = harder, more precise drawing); startHint 1 rings the stars a solution must start from (easier).
- relax: puzzleDifficulty 0-0.3, snapRadius 35-45, startHint 1.
- focus: puzzleDifficulty 0.4-0.7, snapRadius 20-30, startHint 0.
- grit: puzzleDifficulty 0.75-1, snapRadius 15-25, startHint 0; turn startHint on after three or more TRY_FAILED in one round.
- joy: puzzleDifficulty 0.2-0.5, snapRadius 35-40, startHint 0, so rounds are solved often but still need a little thought.
Several TRY_FAILED or TRY_ABANDON in one round mean it is too hard: turn startHint on first, then lower puzzleDifficulty by 0.25. TRY_SOLVED on the first try several rounds running means it is too easy: raise puzzleDifficulty by 0.25.
skill_adjustment_instructions:
Star Puzzles trains Planning (choosing an order that uses every line), Deduction (working out that a one-stroke path has to start at a star with an odd number of lines) and Visualization (tracing the path ahead in the figure).
- planning: puzzleDifficulty 0.5-1 with startHint 0, so long figures must be planned before drawing.
- deduction: startHint 0 at any puzzleDifficulty; turn it on only after repeated TRY_FAILED, as a worked example.
- visualization: puzzleDifficulty 0.5-1 with snapRadius 30-45, so the challenge is the figure, not the drawing precision.
notes: Star Puzzles' difficulty knobs, matching static/skillprintShim.js, ../parameters.json and GameAdjustmentTester's 'star-puzzles' keys.
